title: Set weather-alert display and notification policy
summary: Review severity and delivery-hour controls, save a display threshold, verify the stored policy, and distinguish policy from an active weather feed.
prerequisites: Authorized access to Weather Alerts and its Settings page in a separate fictional training department.
Department agreement on weather-alert display, notifications and call context before operational enablement.

scenes.title: Open Weather Alerts settings
scenes.narration: Open your department’s Weather Alerts page, then select Settings beside View History. This training department currently says there are no active weather alerts. The Settings page opens Notification Settings, which describes the controls for automatically generating messages to department members. This lesson prepares and checks those policy settings. Practice in a separate training department before changing how a live team receives information.
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Choose the display threshold deliberately
scenes.narration: Review Enable Weather Alerts and Minimum Severity to Display. The enable checkbox stays clear throughout this exercise. Change the display selection from Moderate to Severe. The help below says that only alerts at or above the selected severity will be shown in the dashboard. This is the display threshold. The separate table below controls which severities generate automatic messages, so review both areas when deciding your department’s policy.
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Understand severity delivery windows
scenes.narration: Scroll to the complete Auto-Message Severity Threshold table. It provides Extreme, Severe, Moderate, Minor and Unknown rows, each with its own Enabled checkbox, Start Hour and End Hour. Every Enabled box remains clear here. The Extreme row contains eighteen and six: the help explains that this wraps overnight, from six P M to six A M in department local time. Delivery includes the start hour and excludes the end hour. Zero and twenty-four represent all-day delivery. Entered hours alone do not check a row’s Enabled box.
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Separate event exclusions from display
scenes.narration: Review Excluded Alert Events below the table. The help asks for a comma-separated list of event titles that should not generate automatic messages, and says those alerts can still appear in the dashboard. This example retains only a clearly fictional Practice alert title. Treat exclusion as a deliberate messaging decision, not as a way to remove an alert from every view. Agree the appropriate event titles with your department before changing a live policy.
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Review the call-context option
scenes.narration: Below the exclusions, find Attach Weather Context to Calls. Its help says that enabling it attaches active weather alerts near a call’s location as a call note. Keep it unchecked in this training exercise. Consider whether that context belongs in your department’s incident record and review the resulting notes when you test an operational configuration. This recording changes no call notes; it shows the actual option and its stated purpose.
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Save and verify the stored threshold
scenes.narration: Select Save Settings for the prepared policy. Reload Settings and look at Minimum Severity to Display again: Severe remains selected. Enable Weather Alerts is still unchecked. That fresh readback confirms the threshold was stored beyond the earlier unsaved dropdown choice. It does not demonstrate a received weather alert or a delivered message. Verify the saved controls and any operational results separately.
scenes.practice: Save and verify the stored threshold
scenes.capture_intent: Show each actual control and distinguish prepared, validated, saved and executed states.

scenes.title: Restore and reopen the training policy
scenes.narration: Return the display selection to Moderate and select Save Settings again. The page shows Settings saved successfully beside the button. Reload once more: Moderate is retained, and global Enable Weather Alerts remains clear. Scroll through the full severity table to confirm its unchecked rows and retained hours. Then review the unchanged fictional exclusion and unchecked call-context control. This leaves the original disabled training policy in place.
scenes.practice: Restore and reopen the training policy

scenes.title: Validate the feed separately for your department
required_labels: No weather alert sources configured. Add a source to start receiving weather alerts.
scenes.narration: The Alert Sources notice says no weather alert sources are configured. Saving notification policy does not establish a live feed. Source setup and a verified alert are separate work before operational use. Search-and-rescue teams, wildland contractors, industrial emergency teams and security departments can all benefit from an agreed weather-information policy, as can community paramedicine, mental health response, fire and E M S teams. Choose the display and messaging behavior that supports your operations, then test the complete configured service.

scope_limits: Source proposal only; actual speech generation, listening, complete correspondence, encoded-frame review and playback qualification remain required.

Only the disabled notification policy was changed and reopened. Minimum Severity to Display changed Moderate to Severe, saved successfully, and retained Severe after reload; it was then restored to Moderate, saved with visible success and independently reopened. Global alerts, all five auto-message severity enables and call integration remained unchecked. Extreme hours18to6, other rows0to24 and the fictional excluded title were retained and read back. No source was added or activated. The Add/Edit Source form has a default checked Active field but is unsaved and has no configured source; it is never called an enabled feed. Existing Guid source/zone materialization failure remains unresolved outside this policy-only exercise. No live weather receipt, display filtering effect on real alerts, message delivery, call-note creation, zone management or forecast result is claimed.
